recommendations.text: In the first 5 minutes, stabilize the patient, check glucose, and prepare for benzodiazepine administration. Time is critical - status epilepticus becomes progressively harder to treat.

For Initial Stabilization (T=0-5 min), the following actions are mandatory: - assess airway breathing circulation (within 2 minutes) - check point of care glucose (within 5 minutes) - establish iv access (within 5 minutes) - assess seizure semiology

During Initial Stabilization (T=0-5 min), the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give phenytoin as first line, give valproate as first line, restrain patient forcefully, place oral airway during seizure.

Hypoglycemia can cause seizures and must be corrected before or simultaneously with antiepileptic therapy; dextrose 50% IV push. [BEFORE: give_dextrose_50_percent, give_benzodiazepine] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Hypoglycemic seizures resolve with glucose correction; antiepileptics are ineffective and delay definitive treatment. [FORBIDDEN: give_antiepileptic_before_glucose_correction, delay_glucose_correction_for_eeg] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: NCS Status Epilepticus 2012; hypoglycemic seizures resolve with glucose correction, not antiepileptics

recommendations.text: Patients with known epilepsy may have subtherapeutic drug levels triggering SE; levels guide reload decisions. [REQUIRED: check_antiepileptic_drug_levels] (Severity: MODERATE)

Loading a new AED without checking existing levels risks toxicity if existing drug is therapeutic or over-therapeutic. [FORBIDDEN: add_new_aed_without_checking_levels, give_loading_dose_without_level_check] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: NCS Status Epilepticus 2012; subtherapeutic levels require optimization before adding new agents

recommendations.text: Benzodiazepines are the initial therapy of choice: IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (max 4 mg), IM midazolam 10 mg for >40 kg, or IV diazepam 0.15 mg/kg (max 10 mg). A single repeat dose may be given if seizures persist after 5 minutes.
For First-Line Benzodiazepine Therapy (T=5-20 min), the following actions are mandatory: - give benzodiazepine first line (within 10 minutes) - monitor respiratory status (within 5 minutes)

During First-Line Benzodiazepine Therapy (T=5-20 min), the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give phenytoin as first line, give valproate as first line, give levetiracetam as first line, delay benzodiazepine, give propofol as first line.
Alcohol withdrawal SE requires higher benzodiazepine doses due to GABA receptor downregulation; standard doses are often insufficient. [REQUIRED: give_benzodiazepine_high_dose] (Severity: HIGH)

Phenytoin is ineffective for alcohol withdrawal seizures (mechanism is GABA not sodium channel); haloperidol lowers seizure threshold. [FORBIDDEN: give_phenytoin_in_alcohol_withdrawal_seizure, give_haloperidol_in_withdrawal_seizure] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: NCS Status Epilepticus 2012; phenytoin is ineffective for alcohol withdrawal seizures; haloperidol lowers seizure threshold

recommendations.text: If seizures persist after adequate benzodiazepine dosing, give one of: fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg IV, valproate 40 mg/kg IV, or levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV. The ESETT trial showed equivalent efficacy among these three agents.
For Second-Line AED Therapy (T=20-40 min), the following actions are mandatory: - give second line antiepileptic (within 30 minutes) - continuous eeg monitoring (within 30 minutes)

During Second-Line AED Therapy (T=20-40 min), the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give benzodiazepine as second line, delay second line agent, give oral antiepileptic.

Valproate is teratogenic (Category X) causing neural tube defects in 6-9% of exposed pregnancies; absolutely contraindicated. [FORBIDDEN: give_valproate, give_valproate_40mg_kg, give_valproic_acid] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AES 2024 Section 4.3; FDA Black Box Warning; Meador KJ, NEJM 2009

recommendations.text: Valproate is hepatotoxic and contraindicated in significant liver disease; can cause fatal hepatic failure. [FORBIDDEN: give_valproate, give_valproate_40mg_kg, give_valproic_acid] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AES 2024 Section 4.3; FDA Black Box Warning

recommendations.text: Elderly patients require reduced phenytoin/fosphenytoin loading (15 mg PE/kg instead of 20) due to altered pharmacokinetics and increased cardiovascular risk. [FORBIDDEN: give_full_dose_phenytoin, give_fosphenytoin_20mg_pe_kg] (Severity: HIGH)

Phenytoin/fosphenytoin causes cardiac arrhythmias and hypotension via sodium channel blockade; contraindicated in pre-existing cardiac conduction disease. [FORBIDDEN: give_phenytoin, give_fosphenytoin_20mg_pe_kg] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Phenytoin, valproate, and phenobarbital are porphyrinogenic; they induce hepatic ALA synthase and can trigger fatal acute porphyria attacks. [FORBIDDEN: give_phenytoin, give_fosphenytoin_20mg_pe_kg, give_valproate, give_valproate_40mg_kg, give_phenobarbital_15mg_kg] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AES 2024 Section 4.6; Anderson KE, Ann Intern Med 2005

recommendations.text: Refractory SE requires intubation, ICU admission, and continuous IV anesthetic (midazolam, propofol, or pentobarbital) titrated to EEG burst suppression. Ketamine is an emerging option for super-refractory SE.

For Refractory Status Epilepticus (T>40 min), the following actions are mandatory: - perform endotracheal intubation (within 45 minutes) - initiate continuous iv anesthetic (within 50 minutes) - continuous eeg monitoring - admit to icu (within 50 minutes)

During Refractory Status Epilepticus (T>40 min), the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge home, give oral antiepileptic only, discontinue eeg monitoring, extubate during active se.
Continuous EEG monitoring should be maintained for at least 24 hours after seizure cessation. Maintenance AED should be started before weaning the continuous infusion.
For Ongoing Monitoring and AED Transition, the following actions are mandatory: - continuous eeg monitoring - initiate maintenance antiepileptic (within 120 minutes) - reassess neurological status

During Ongoing Monitoring and AED Transition, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discontinue eeg prematurely, rapid anesthetic wean, discharge without neurology followup.

key_sections.overview: Time-phased management of convulsive status epilepticus from initial stabilization through refractory treatment Key evidence: Each minute of untreated SE reduces probability of seizure termination by 5%; benzodiazepines effective in 60-80% if given within first 5 minutes (Treiman DM, NEJM 1998)

Time is critical - status epilepticus becomes progressively harder to treat. Hypoglycemic seizures resolve with glucose correction; antiepileptics are ineffective and delay definitive treatment. Patients with known epilepsy may have subtherapeutic drug levels triggering SE; levels guide reload decisions. Loading a new AED without checking existing levels risks toxicity if existing drug is therapeutic or over-therapeutic.

A single repeat dose may be given if seizures persist after 5 minutes. The ESETT trial showed equivalent efficacy among these three agents. Required actions: give_second_line_antiepileptic, continuous_eeg_monitoring Contraindicated: give_benzodiazepine_as_second_line, delay_second_line_agent, give_oral_antiepileptic Valproate is teratogenic (Category X) causing neural tube defects in 6-9% of exposed pregnancies; absolutely contraindicated. Valproate is hepatotoxic and contraindicated in significant liver disease; can cause fatal hepatic failure. Elderly patients require reduced phenytoin/fosphenytoin loading (15 mg PE/kg instead of 20) due to altered pharmacokinetics and increased cardiovascular risk. key_sections.refractory_status_epilepticus_(t>40_min): Continuous IV anesthetic infusion with EEG monitoring for seizures persisting despite first and second-line therapy Guideline states: Refractory SE requires intubation, ICU admission, and continuous IV anesthetic (midazolam, propofol, or pentobarbital) titrated to EEG burst suppression. Ketamine is an emerging option for super-refractory SE. Required actions: perform_endotracheal_intubation, initiate_continuous_iv_anesthetic, continuous_eeg_monitoring, admit_to_icu Contraindicated: discharge_home, give_oral_antiepileptic_only, discontinue_eeg_monitoring, extubate_during_active_se
key_sections.ongoing_monitoring_and_aed_transition: Continuous EEG monitoring, maintenance AED initiation, and gradual anesthetic wean Guideline states: Continuous EEG monitoring should be maintained for at least 24 hours after seizure cessation. Maintenance AED should be started before weaning the continuous infusion. Required actions: continuous_eeg_monitoring, initiate_maintenance_antiepileptic, reassess_neurological_status Contraindicated: discontinue_eeg_prematurely, rapid_anesthetic_wean, discharge_without_neurology_followup
